material_systems.name: Exterior Acrylic Primer for Wood/FC Porch Ceiling

products: Benjamin Moore Ultra Spec EXT Primer
PPG Sun Proof Exterior Latex Primer
primer.notes: Standard 100% acrylic exterior primer for (1) bare wood porch ceiling — full field prime and (2) factory-primed fiber cement — field prime over factory transit primer (MANDATORY per James Hardie warranty). Coverage lower than vertical application due to overhead waste factor (~10%). Must be top-coated within 180 days on fiber cement.

material_systems.notes: Shared system — same product covers both bare wood and factory-primed FC. Factory-primed FC has lower porosity (higher end of coverage range). Bare wood T&G/beadboard has higher absorption (lower end). Apply surface_texture_modifier for rough-sawn boards.

material_systems.name: Alkyd/Shellac Spot Primer for Tannin Knots on Wood Porch Ceiling

products: KILZ Original Multi-Surface Stain Blocking Primer
primer.notes: Spot-applied to visible knots on tannin-rich species (cedar, redwood, Douglas fir) BEFORE full acrylic primer coat. Not a full-surface system — applied per knot/stain location by brush. Tannin bleed is especially visible on flat white and haint blue porch ceilings.

material_systems.notes: Conditional on wood species — required for tannin-rich species (cedar, redwood, fir). Applied by brush to individual knots overhead.

material_systems.name: Alkali-Resistant Primer for Bare Fiber Cement Porch Ceiling

products: Benjamin Moore Ultra Spec Masonry & Stucco Primer
primer.notes: Required for bare/damaged fiber cement porch ceiling panels (pH 13.0). Prevents saponification. Lower coverage than standard acrylic — bare FC is more porous. Overhead application adds waste factor.

material_systems.notes: Bare FC uses SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD by convention when factory primer is absent/damaged.

material_systems.name: Standard Exterior Acrylic Porch Ceiling Paint

finish.notes: Standard residential exterior acrylic. Flat to satin sheen. QT2 single coat on primed surfaces. QT3 requires 2 coats. Mildew-resistant formulation critical for sheltered porch ceiling — doubly sheltered from UV means higher mildew risk. Haint blue and white are the most common porch ceiling colors.

material_systems.notes: Flat is the most common porch ceiling sheen. Overhead application requires thin coats to prevent sag.

material_systems.name: Premium Exterior Acrylic Porch Ceiling Paint

finish.type: Premium 100% Acrylic Exterior with Enhanced Mildew Resistance
finish.notes: Premium materials with superior color retention and mildew resistance. Light sand between coats (220-grit). Premium formulation has higher solids — slightly lower coverage per gallon.

material_systems.notes: Premium finish for QT4. Mildew-resistant formulation is especially important for sheltered porch ceilings.

SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD.notes: Bare wood T&G, beadboard, or plywood porch ceiling. Moderate-to-high absorption. Overhead waste included.

SS_EXT_PRIMED_FACTORY.notes: Factory-primed fiber cement — sealed surface, lower absorption. Overhead waste included.

coverage_profiles.overhead_waste_notes: 10% additional material waste for overhead application. Already factored into sf_per_gallon rates.
assumptions: Coverage rates include overhead waste factor — do not apply again at runtime.
Surface_texture_modifier applies on top of base coverage for rough-sawn T&G/beadboard boards.
Spray application: multiply material quantity by 1.25-1.40 for transfer efficiency loss.

SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD.notes: Bare/damaged fiber cement porch ceiling (using SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD by convention). Highly porous. Overhead waste included.

SYS_EXT_PRCH_FINISH_STANDARD.notes: Standard acrylic on primed porch ceiling surface. Overhead waste included.

SYS_EXT_PRCH_FINISH_PREMIUM.notes: Premium acrylic has higher solids — slightly lower coverage. Overhead waste included.

assumptions: Coverage is per NET porch ceiling area from PaintScope (PS_EXT_SURFACE_SF.PORCH_CEILING).
Two-coat system is standard at QT3/QT4. QT2 may use single coat.
Spray application: multiply material quantity by 1.25-1.40 for transfer efficiency loss.
T&G/beadboard boards: apply surface_texture_modifier 1.15 for rough-sawn texture.

consumables.name: 80-120 Grit Sandpaper for Wood Porch Ceiling Prep
consumables.notes: 80-120 grit for wood adhesion profile. Overhead use increases consumption. Hand blocks for T&G/beadboard grooves, orbital sander for flat panels.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 220 Grit
consumables.notes: Intercoat sanding at QT4 between finish coats. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 150 Grit
consumables.notes: Scuff sand fiber cement porch ceiling panels. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Tack Cloth
consumables.notes: Dust removal after sanding. Overhead work causes more dust to fall — tack cloth pass ensures clean substrate. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Fiber Cement End-Cut Edge Sealer
consumables.notes: Seal field-cut edges on fiber cement porch ceiling panels to prevent capillary moisture absorption.

consumables.name: Exterior Flexible Paintable Caulk for Porch Ceiling Joints
consumables.notes: Polyurethane or siliconized acrylic for panel joints and ceiling-to-fascia/wall junctions. Overhead caulking is slower. Caulk AFTER primer coat.

consumables.name: Angled Sash Brush 2.5 inch
consumables.notes: Primary brush for detail — cut-in at junctions, T&G/beadboard groove work, knot spot-priming. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Flat Brush 3 inch
consumables.notes: Secondary brush for wider T&G/beadboard groove channels.

consumables.name: 9-inch Roller Cover for Overhead Porch Ceiling
consumables.notes: 3/8-inch nap for smooth panels. 1/2-inch nap for T&G/beadboard. Higher consumption overhead (300 SF vs 500 SF vertical).

consumables.name: Extension Pole for Overhead Roller Application
consumables.notes: 4-8 ft extension pole for overhead roller work. Primary tool for porch ceiling application.

consumables.name: Airless Spray Tip 413 for Porch Ceiling
consumables.notes: 413-515 tip for porch ceiling spray. Always eligible (no vent constraint like soffit).

consumables.name: 60-Mesh Spray Filter for Latex
consumables.notes: Standard 60-mesh filter for latex through airless equipment. Only when spray method.

consumables.name: Plastic Sheeting for Porch Floor/Furniture Protection
consumables.notes: 4 mil minimum for porch floor and furniture protection. Critical for overhead work — all drips fall onto porch floor.

consumables.name: Canvas Drop Cloths
consumables.usage_rate: 1 EA per 100 SF porch floor coverage
consumables.notes: Heavy canvas for porch floor. Non-slip for crew traffic. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Painter's Tape (exterior grade)
consumables.notes: UV-resistant exterior masking tape for fascia/wall junction masking and fixture protection. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Masking Film/Paper for Adjacent Fascia/Wall
consumables.notes: Masking film for protecting finished fascia and wall from roller spatter. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Caulk Gun
consumables.notes: Standard caulk gun. Overhead caulking requires good trigger control.

ext_porch_floor.description: Porch floor directly below ceiling work zone — primary drip fallout area
ext_porch_floor.notes: CRITICAL for overhead work. All drips fall directly onto porch floor. Canvas drop cloths provide non-slip crew traffic surface. Spray mode requires full plastic coverage.

ext_porch_furniture.description: Porch furniture, planters, swings below ceiling work area
ext_porch_furniture.notes: Cover with plastic sheeting or remove from porch before overhead work begins. Removal is preferred when feasible.

ext_light_fixture.description: Porch ceiling-mounted fixtures — ceiling fans, pendant lights, recessed cans
ext_light_fixture.notes: Ceiling fans: remove blades if possible, or mask mounting plate and blade edges. Pendant lights: bag fixture. Recessed cans: tape ring and trim.

ext_fascia_adjacent.description: Fascia board at porch roof edge — protect when already finished
ext_fascia_adjacent.notes: Tape + masking film at fascia-ceiling junction when fascia is already painted. Quantity derived from ceiling perimeter LF.

ext_wall_adjacent.description: House wall at porch attachment — protect when already finished
ext_wall_adjacent.notes: Tape at ceiling-to-wall junction when house siding/wall is already painted. Protect to prevent roller spatter on finished wall.

compatibility_rules.description: Acrylic primer for bare wood and factory-primed fiber cement porch ceiling
compatibility_rules.notes: Field prime on FC is MANDATORY per Hardie warranty.

compatibility_rules.description: Alkali-resistant primer required for bare fiber cement porch ceiling
compatibility_rules.notes: Bare FC (pH 13.0) causes saponification with standard acrylic primer.

compatibility_rules.description: No primer needed when substrate is field-primed
compatibility_rules.notes: Skip prime module entirely when already field-primed.

compatibility_rules.description: Flat and satin sheen only for porch ceiling
compatibility_rules.notes: Overhead surfaces show imperfections at higher sheen.

compatibility_rules.description: Caulk AFTER primer coat — never before
compatibility_rules.notes: Caulk adheres better to primed surfaces. Sequence: prep -> prime -> caulk -> finish.

compatibility_rules.description: No power washing on porch ceiling
compatibility_rules.notes: High-pressure power washing damages thin panel edges, strips factory primer. Low-pressure wash only (garden hose + soft brush).

risk_notes.topic: Tannin bleed-through on wood porch ceiling
risk_notes.risk: Cedar/redwood T&G/beadboard porch ceiling boards bleed tannins. Brown staining visible on flat white and haint blue finishes.
risk_notes.mitigation: Spot-prime all visible knots with alkyd/shellac stain blocker before full primer.

risk_notes.topic: Mildew growth on sheltered porch ceiling
risk_notes.risk: Porch ceilings are doubly sheltered — ideal mildew habitat in humid climates.
risk_notes.mitigation: Use paint with mildewcide. Clean with mildewcide solution before painting.

risk_notes.risk: Overhead application causes drips and sags onto porch floor and furniture.
risk_notes.mitigation: Thin coats. Back-brush after rolling. Extension pole for consistent pressure. Protect all surfaces below.

risk_notes.topic: Edge wicking on fiber cement panels
risk_notes.risk: Unsealed field-cut edges absorb moisture via cellulose capillaries.
risk_notes.mitigation: Seal ALL field-cut edges with end-cut sealer.

material_quantity_notes.overhead_waste_factor: All coverage rates include ~10% overhead waste factor. Do NOT apply additional overhead waste at runtime.
material_quantity_notes.surface_texture_factor: T&G/beadboard rough-sawn boards: multiply quantity by 1.15x. Smooth panels: 1.00x.
material_quantity_notes.spray_transfer_efficiency: Airless spray on porch ceiling: 60-75% transfer efficiency (slightly better than soffit due to no vent concern). Multiply coverage by 1.25-1.40.
material_quantity_notes.two_coat_standard: Standard: 1 prime + 2 finish at QT3/QT4. Field-primed skips prime. QT2 single finish coat.
material_quantity_notes.tg_beadboard_joint_note: T&G and beadboard groove surface area is captured in the surface_texture_modifier. Do not double-count.

assumptions.source: Sibling SF_SOFFIT_EXT_NC_v1 materials.json, adjusted for same overhead conditions

assumptions.value: No vinyl bonding primer or solar-reflective finish system needed
assumptions.source: Porch ceilings use wood or fiber cement, not vinyl

assumptions.value: Beadboard coverage factor same as T&G (1.15x texture modifier)
assumptions.source: Beadboard grooves are functionally equivalent to T&G for painting material consumption

uncertainty_flags.description: Porch ceiling spray transfer efficiency estimated at 60-75% (better than soffit due to no vent concern but still overhead). Limited field data.
